scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

prediction.raw: **1 (Yes, you're the asshole)** **Why:** - **You asked him to step into a parental role without his consent.** He’s not your son’s biological father, nor do you live together. While it’s kind for partners to occasionally help with childcare, *demanding* it as a " small stuff" expectation after 3 years in a non cohabiting relationship is unreasonable. He’s not obligated to be a substitute parent. - **The biological father is the primary responsible party.** His dad lives nearby (South London) and *could* transport him, even if it’s a longer commute. It’s not his job to solve your logistics problem when the biological parent is available (even if inconvenient). - **You mischaracterized his contributions.** You claimed he was "working longer hours to support [you and your son]," but *you* extended *your own* work hours to afford football. He didn’t agree to financially support you or your son—he’s simply working his standard 7am–7pm job. - **"Part of the family" is a loaded phrase.** Telling him " if he’s part of the family, he wouldn’t mind" pressures him to adopt a role he hasn’t agreed to. Relationships evolve organically; you can’t force someone to " be family" on your terms. - **His boundaries are valid.** After a grueling work week, he’s entitled to weekends for rest. asking him to chauffeur your child *every* weekend (especially when he’s not cohabiting) is a significant ask that crossed his personal boundaries. **What you should do:** - **Respect his decision to break up.** This isn’t about " a bloody football game"— it’s about clear communication and mutual respect for boundaries. - **Take responsibility:** Focus on solutions *you* control (e.g., carpooling with other parents, adjusting your work schedule, or discussing with your ex-partner). - **Learn from this:** In relationships, *ask* for help, don’t demand it. Frame requests as "Would you be willing..." not "You *must* do this because I need it." > ️ **Note:** AITA scenarios often hinge on *contextual fairness*. While your son’s needs matter, his well-being doesn’t justify overstepping your partner’s autonomy. The fact that your *mum* agreed with him reinforces that this was a boundary violation. > **Final verdict: 1 (Yes, you’re the asshole)**. > *— This is a neutral analysis based on common relationship dynamics and societal expectations. Always prioritize open communication and mutual respect in partnerships.* 😊
